events.title: Anne Boleyn Is Crowned Queen of England
events.description: In a lavish ceremony, Anne Boleyn was crowned queen consort of England. She was the second wife of Henry VIII, and the coronation followed his break with the Catholic Church in order to marry her.
events.significance: The coronation marked a turning point in the English Reformation. Her daughter, Elizabeth I, later became one of England's most celebrated monarchs.

events.title: The Glorious First of June
events.description: British and French fleets fought in the Atlantic, far from the coast of Ushant. It was the first major naval clash between the two powers in the French Revolutionary Wars.
events.significance: Britain claimed a tactical victory, but a vital French grain convoy reached port. The battle showed how the war at sea would unfold over the next two decades.

events.title: Tennessee Becomes the 16th U.S. State
events.description: Tennessee was admitted to the Union. It was the first state formed from territory south of the Ohio River.
events.significance: Its statehood marked the westward growth of the young United States. Tennessee later became central to the country's history in the Civil War and in American music.

events.title: BOAC Flight 777 Is Shot Down
events.description: German Junkers Ju 88 fighters shot down a civilian airliner over the Bay of Biscay. All aboard were killed, including the British actor Leslie Howard, star of 'Gone with the Wind'.
events.significance: The loss of a beloved film star shocked the Allied public. Historians still debate why the unarmed plane was targeted.

events.title: CNN Begins Broadcasting
events.description: Cable News Network launched as the first channel devoted to news around the clock. Its first broadcast was in the United States.
events.significance: CNN changed how people follow events as they unfold. It helped create the modern 24-hour news cycle.
